newsitem.title: GERMANY: London holiday, softer U.S. market push Bunds lower.
newsitem.headline: London holiday, softer U.S. market push Bunds lower.

text.p: German Bunds slipped lower in quiet trading shaped by the absence of London's traders celebrating a bank holiday and U.S. dealers' anticipation of upcoming new supply and worries about rising interest rates.
Bunds were down 22 basis points at 97.20 near the end of trading on Monday having traded between 97.12 and 97.32.

Lacking London's volume as market participants were enjoying a long weekend, Frankfurt dealers said trading was particularly lacklustre with most people waiting for the day to end. "Even the numbers released today did not move the market significantly," a dealer said.
News that pan-German producer prices were unchanged in July from June and were down 0.8 percent on the year did not move the market much, dealers said.
Similarly news that German inflation numbers for August were largely in line with expecations also failed to give the market a move in either direction.

Early in the day the state of Bavaria reported its consumer prices had fallen 0.1 percent on the month and were up 1.3 percent on the year. Preliminary August prices in West Germany were down 0.1 percent on the month and were up 1.4 percent on the year.
In the U.S. dealers were worried about that the sale of two-year notes on Tuesday and three-year notes on Wednesday will keep the negative price bias intact.
Dealers were also slightly nervous that interest rates would soon begin creeping higher in the U.S. even though rates were left unchanged last Thursday.

In Germany the Bundesbank's unexpectedly large interest rate cut last Thursday when the central council lowered its repo rate by 30 basis points to three percent, has eliminated most hopes for another German easing, dealers said. "We may just be trading around here for a while," one added.
